subject: Post-call: performance guardrails & reserved-slab sizing for Streamline.ai
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@streamline.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@streamline.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance guardrails & reserved-slab sizing for Streamline.ai

Thanks again for the call earlier — great context on the real-time summarization use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on acceptance criteria for a reserved-capacity validation.

Key behavioral targets you asked about (please confirm):
- Streaming scenario: average prompt length ~ 120 tokens, typical response 90 tokens, peak burst to 10 concurrent streams per instance.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end token emission latency <= 180ms at baseline load; p99 soft target <= 400ms under sustained concurrency.
- Throughput: steady-state 12 requests/sec (QPS) with occasional bursts up to 40 QPS for 90s windows.
- Concurrency: plan for sustained 40 concurrent inference contexts across the reserved slab with autoscale for short bursts.

What we need from you to size reserved slab and propose GPU mix:
1) A representative traffic profile (sample timestamps + token counts) — Raj, thanks for offering to send this; the streamline-traffic-profile.json attachment works well.
2) A short evaluation prompt set (10–20 representative prompts) so we can sanity-check quality/regression with quantized runs.
3) Confirmation of regulatory constraints (data residency, logs retention) that might affect on-prem vs dedicated routing.

Our proposed validation plan (high level):
- Run synthetic streaming load that mirrors your profile (prefix priming to exercise KV cache).
- Compare two reserved-slab options: H100-based slab (higher single-request throughput) vs A100-80GB mixed slab (better cost/throughput balance for batchy flows).
- Measure: p50/p95/p99 token emission latency, tokens/sec per GPU, memory headroom for quantized models, and percentage of requests hitting autoscale fallback.
- Acceptance: p95 <= 180ms and sustained reserved throughput >= 12 QPS without fallback for 30m window.

I attached a short post-call summary (streamline-postcall-notes.pdf) and our sample runbook draft. If that acceptance noise-floor looks right, we’ll schedule a dedicated-capacity validation next week and lock in a short reserved slab for a 72-hour pilot.

Next steps
- Raj: send traffic sample and confirm data residency constraints (by EOD Mon).
- Alyssa: share 10 representative prompts you want included in the quality checks.
- Karthik/Marissa (internal): I’ll need a quick sizing sketch so we can confirm GPU shortlist ahead of the run.

Thanks — Sergio

--
Sergio Alvarez

Date: Mon, 11 Sep 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance guardrails & reserved-slab sizing for Streamline.ai

Thanks Sergio — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side:

Confirmed targets (we’re aligned):
- Streaming flows as discussed (median prompt ~120 tokens, median response ~95 tokens).
- Aim for p95 <= 180ms; p99 <= 450ms at peak.
- Steady QPS ~12, bursts up to 45 QPS for ~1.5m at most during ingest windows.
- Concurrency expectation: 35–45 concurrent user streams across the reservation.

I've attached a sanitized traffic profile (streamline-traffic-profile.json) with timestamped token counts and an engineers contact for procurement. On legal/procurement, Raj (cc) is leading procurement and will share the PO cadence.

We don’t have special residency constraints — US-only is fine for this validation. For the prompt set, I’ll drop 15 representative prompts into the Drive link you shared by EOD today.

If you want to kick off the reserved-slab pilot the week of Sep 17, that works for us — please send the proposed slot options.

Best,
Alyssa

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Streamline reserved-slab sizing sketch + quick technical asks

Karthik/Marissa — Alyssa sent their traffic sample and confirmed targets. I sketched two reservation options; need your quick take plus whether we can meet acceptance without overspending.

Customer constraints / workload notes
- Median tokens/request ~215 total (prompt+response). Streaming mode; frequent long-lived contexts to keep KV cache warm.
- Steady 12 QPS, burst up to 45 QPS for up to 90–120s; concurrency target 40 sustained contexts.

Candidate slabs (shortlist):
Option A: H100 slab (4x H100)
- Expected steady throughput: ~18–22 QPS for the model variant in fp16 streaming with modest batching.
- Pros: single-request latency headroom, better for elastic bursts.
- Cons: higher hourly cost.

Option B: Mixed A100-80GB slab (6x A100-80GB)
- Expected steady throughput: ~14–18 QPS; better cost per token for sustained workloads and larger batch memory.
- Pros: cost-efficient for sustained 12 QPS without frequent autoscale.
- Cons: weaker p99 under tight burst unless we provision more reserve.

Quantization considerations:
- 8-bit quant (INT8) looks viable for their promptset but we should run a 10-prompt quality check (do we have that set? Alyssa said she will upload).
- Plan: compare fp16 vs int8 latency and token quality; prefer int8 for cost unless quality regression > 2% BLEU-like metric on our eval.

Proposed validation runbook (short):
1) Warm-up: prime KV cache with their sample prompts (30min).
2) Baseline run: steady 12 QPS for 60m, measure p50/p95/p99 token latency.
3) Burst run: step to 45 QPS for 90s, repeat 6x with 2m recovery between bursts.
4) Stress/scale test: sustained 40 concurrent contexts for 30m and measure model memory pressure and %fallback events.
5) Quality check: run 15 prompts against fp16 and int8.

Acceptance criteria (suggested)
- p95 <= 180ms during baseline; p99 <= 450ms during bursts.
- No more than 5% of requests result in autoscale fallback over whole run.
- Int8 quality regression <= 2% vs fp16 on the provided prompt set.

Can you quick sanity-check the slab sizing and whether we should recommend Option B with a short burst buffer (x2 burst credits) or go H100 for simpler acceptance? I’ll sync with Alyssa on slots once we decide.

Thanks — Sergio
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Streamline reserved-slab sizing sketch + quick technical asks

This looks good. My quick read: Option B (A100 slab) is the better commercial fit if they truly sustain 12 QPS and only need short burst windows; recommend we provision an additional 15–20% burst buffer as a temporary guardrail during the pilot.

Operational asks before we commit:
- Confirm model variant and tokenizer; if customers use longer context windows (>= 2k) we should increase memory headroom.
- We'll want to run the int8 quality check first; if regression is marginal (<=2%) we go int8 else fp16 default.
- Logistics: I'll schedule a 90m kickoff with their engineers on Sep 18 or 19 — Sergio, send two possible slots and I’ll assemble the infra team.

I’ll also prepare a short runbook with exact CLI commands for the team and add it to the Drive link (reserved-slab-runbook-draft.md).

—Marissa
